claims.claim_text: The indexed Captain Roderick G.S. Hall is Roderick Stephen Hall, who signed his 1943 OSS proposal as R.S.G. Hall.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The full indexed name and initials align with an official biography reproducing Hall's signed proposal, Army unit, grade, location, and direct OSS response.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by the exact initials and full name, compatible rank progression, Army unit, and direct official OSS correspondence.
claims.temporal_assessment: The official account dates the proposal to fall 1943 and places his Army engineer assignment immediately before OSS ordered him to Washington.
claims.match_notes: Stephen, Steve, and R.S.G. are preserved as documented variants; the indexed Roderick G.S. form remains primary.

claims.claim_text: Hall's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was the U.S. Army's 270th Engineer Combat Battalion at Camp Adair.
claims.evidence_excerpt: 2nd Lt. 270 Engr. (c) Bn. / Camp Adair, Oregon
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Hall's 1943 proposal supplies the unit and location; the official account says OSS answered by ordering him to Washington.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed within the same signed official correspondence.
claims.match_notes: The later Captain rank in the personnel index is preserved separately from the second-lieutenant grade in the 1943 letter.

claims.claim_text: Hall was a Yale University student before he left school to enlist in the Army.

claims.evidence_paraphrase: CIA explicitly sequences Yale enrollment, withdrawal, and Army enlistment after Pearl Harbor.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed within the same exact-name official biography and signed-letter record.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded before Army and OSS service; it is student status, not employment.
claims.match_notes: No reliable named civilian employer has yet been identified in the accessible sources reviewed.
